  "name": "rolling",

  "cwd": ".",

  "metric": {"kind": "reported", "direction": "lower_is_better", "unit": "s"},

  "correctness": {
    "command": ["python", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-m", "not deliberately_flaky", "tests/test_rolling.py"],

    "outputs": [{"path": "out/result.npy", "compare": "numbers"}]
  },
  "warmup": 1,
  "budget": {"max_rounds": 60, "max_seconds": 1800},

  "alpha": 0.05,
  "timeout_seconds": 120,
  "harness": ["bench.py"],
  "oracle": ["tests/test_rolling.py"],
  "inputs": [],
  "config": [],
  "allow_runtime_change": false,
  "allow_cross_host": false
}
EOF
perfproof project confirm target-python_cpu bench --json | head -c 600; echo
perfproof project goal bench --metric reported --direction lower_is_better --unit s --confirm --json | head -c 600; echo

import re
s=open('rolling.py').read()
i=s.index("    out = np.empty")
s=s[:i]+'''    prefix = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    np.cumsum(values, dtype=np.int64, out=prefix[1:])
    return prefix[width:] - prefix[: n - width + 1]
'''
s=s.replace("Runs in O(n) time with a running total.","Runs in O(n) time from prefix sums; a prefix sum that wraps around\n    int64 still gives exact window sums, since the wrap cancels.")
open('rolling.py','w').write(s)
EOF
